Subject: Dedicated capacity — questions on SKU mix for long-context clinical models

Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow up as we sketch out our Dedicated ask: our med‑NLP models will run a mixture of long context summarization (up to 128k tokens), nearline batch reranking, and high‑volume embedding generation for search. Expected steady QPS for the first 12 months is ~80 reqs/minute with spiky peaks up to 250 reqs/minute during morning triage windows. Target P99 generation latency under 700ms for short inference paths, and acceptable longer tail for the 128k summarization jobs.

Can you advise a recommended SKU split (H100/A100/L4) and whether we should consolidate onto one pool with slot tiling or run distinct pools per workload? I've attached our anonymized usage profile. Also looping in procurement (procurement@orionhealth.com) to track cadence.

Cheers,
Jacob
Jacob Reed
Head of ML Platform — Orion Health

Attachments: orion_usage_profile.csv (CSV summary of token distribution, QPS, peak windows)

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — questions on SKU mix for long-context clinical models

Jacob —

Appreciate the profile, that makes this concrete. High level recommendation up front: use a mixed‑pool strategy with workload tagging. Short summary:

• Long‑context summarization (128k): H100‑like SKUs (we recommend H100‑class nodes) to avoid OOMs and minimize slow quantization regressions at very long sequence lengths.
• Balanced generation (interactive medium context): A100 class gives the best tokens/$ for mid‑length (up to ~16k) with stable latencies.
• Embeddings & high QPS lightweight traffic: L4 fleet is cost‑effective for high‑concurrency embedding calls and allows very aggressive slotting.

Operationally: run two logical pools — \"heavy\" (H100 + A100 reserved for canary/critical paths) and \"light\" (L4 for bursty embedding load). Use slot tiling and prefix cache on the heavy pool for summarization batching. For cost predictability, we recommend reserving a baseline H100 capacity sized for the sustained summarization throughput (~2–3 concurrent long runs), and autoscale A100 nodes for medium workloads.

I'll loop Ben for the ops runbook and Karthik for deal economics. Draft mutual action plan attached (MVP milestones + procurement touchpoints).

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — questions on SKU mix for long-context clinical models

Quick ops notes from my side:

1) Memory headroom: For 128k token runs we need H100 nodes with 80–90GB usable model memory (depends on quantization). We'll recommend a conservative headroom of ~20% above peak working set to reduce OOM risk.

2) Slotting: heavy pool should use coarse slotting for long jobs (1–2 jobs per GPU with big KV caches) and fine slotting on A100 for medium contexts. L4 pool can use very high slot density (16–24 slots) for embeddings.

3) Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback from H100→A100 for mid‑length jobs only when H100 is saturated; do not fallback 128k summarization to A100 unless we've preemptively checkpointed KV state.

I've sketched an ops runbook (attached as cost‑comparison; it includes expected per‑token cost differences per SKU and rough monthly cost based on the attached profile).

– Ben
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — questions on SKU mix for long-context clinical models

Economics and contract framing:

- Baseline reserved H100 capacity: propose 4 H100 GPUs reserved for the first 12 months (covers ~90% of sustained summarization demand per profile) with annual commit pricing.
- A100 pool: 8 A100 slots as burst capacity (on-demand reserved to a 60% commit factor) to cover medium generation and moderate spikes.
- L4 pool: scale via autoscale groups; no reservation initially — we can cap burst at contract level to control cost.

Estimated blended tokens/$: H100 (long‑context heavy) is highest $/token but required for correctness; A100 is middle ground; L4 is cheapest for embeddings. We'll push a pricing appendix into the MAP so procurement sees per‑unit economics and SLA tradeoffs.

Jacob — if this aligns, procurement steps in the MAP are: 30 day SOW, signature on reserved capacity schedule, and an ops kickoff to finalize exact GPU count after one month of telemetry post‑go‑live.

Karthik Iyer

Thanks — that level of detail is extremely helpful. A few quick decisions from our side:

1) We agree to the mixed‑pool approach.
2) We'll commit to a 12‑month reserved schedule for 4 H100s as proposed, pending final cost appendix.
3) For A100 burst we want a 4‑GPU minimum reservation with the option to scale to 8 after the first month.

Procurement will review the MAP and cost appendix this afternoon; please send the final pricing appendix and the SOW template. Also can you include a note on data residency (we need logs retained 7 years) and an SOC2 evidentiary pointer — procurement will need that for their compliance checklist.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
